::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[What are the advantages and disadvantages between these coding styles?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/20774/what-are-the-advantages-and-disadvantages-between-these-coding-styles), asked by [Display Name](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/2099/display-name) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-06-14; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Some people use the following style
>
> ```latex
> setting
> {
> 	 a=1
> 	,b=2
> 	,c=3	
> }
> ```
>
> and the other ones use the style below 
>
> ```latex
> setting
> {
> 	a=1,
> 	b=2,
> 	c=3	
> }
> ```
>
> I use the latter style but I wonder why some people prefer the former style?
> Is there anything I missed?
:::

Usually when setting keys you can do it this way:

```latex
{
    a=1,
    b=2,
    c=3,
}
```

Then all rows can be commented out and additional rows can be inserted anywhere.
